programme.desc: The misadventures of a suburban boy, family and friends.

programme.desc: The misadventures of two single women in the 1950s and '60s.

programme.title: Inside Edition
programme.desc: Inside Edition featuring investigative reports, interviews with newsmakers, human interest stories, and celebrity and pop-culture features. Hosted by Deborah Norville.

programme.title: Searching for Bobby Fischer

programme.title: DocFilm
programme.desc: The Jasmin Revolution took place in Tunisia in 2010. In 2024, President Kais Saied was re-elected by a large majority. In 2019, he was still seen as a man of integrity and loyal to the constitution. Today, Saied’s ruling style is autocratic.

programme.title: DocFilm

programme.title: Jon Chandonnet
programme.desc: News - Jon Chandonnet was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 1996, and as an active grad student at MIT, he responded by pushing his body to the limits. He ran marathons and climbed mountains to prove MS was not slowing him down. Six years later, that pace caught up with him. In this episode, Mathew Embry talks with Jon about denying the diagnosis, what changed when symptoms hit hard, and how MS demands a different kind of discipline. Jon shares how targeting inflammation through diet and lifestyle became a turning point, and how redefining strength has helped him keep moving forward.
